title: Working with strings
description:
Complete the methods, using the `String` methods from the lesson (no loops needed):

```java
static String initials(String fullName)                 // first and last initial: "ada king lovelace" gives "A.L."
static int countWord(String text, String word)          // how many times word appears in text, ignoring case
static String censor(String text, String word)          // word in lower case, UPPER CASE or Capitalized replaced by * of the same length
static String priceLine(String item, double price)      // item left in 12 characters, price right in 8 with 2 decimals
```

- `initials` ignores spaces around the name, and a single name gives one initial: `"plato"` gives `"P."`.
- `countWord("The cat and the hat. THE end", "the")` is 3. Matches inside other words count too: `countWord("theme", "the")` is 1.
- `censor("Darn, DARN it", "darn")` gives `"****, **** it"`, and `"darned Darn"` becomes `"****ed ****"`. The word can be given in any case.
- `priceLine("Tea", 2.5)` is `"Tea             2.50"`. Use `String.format(Locale.ROOT, ...)`, with `import java.util.Locale;` at the top of the file, so the decimal point is `.` everywhere.
hints: For `initials`, trim the name first. The last initial is the character just after the last space: `lastIndexOf(' ')`, which is -1 when there is no space. A ternary (`condition ? a : b`) picks between one and two initials.

To count without a loop, remove every match with `replace(word, "")` and see how much shorter the text got: each match removed `word.length()` characters. Lower-case both strings first to ignore case.
`"*".repeat(4)` is `"****"`. `replace` is case-sensitive, so call it once for each form of the word: lower case, upper case, and capitalized (first letter upper, the rest lower).
